fact: 1906年4月18日凌晨5时13分，旧金山发生强烈地震；亲历者James B. Stetson记录其在范尼斯大道1801号于5:13被剧烈震动震醒，同期小册子《San Francisco in Ruins》记为“5:13:47”，震动摧毁烟囱与劣质建筑并破坏供水主管，随后引发大面积火灾。

sources.title: James B. Stetson, San Francisco During the Eventful Days of April 1906（Project Gutenberg eBook #4640）
sources.quote: On the morning of April 18, 1906, at 5:13, in my residence, 1801 Van Ness Avenue, I was awakened by a very severe shock of earthquake.

sources.title: A. M. Allison, San Francisco in Ruins（1906年出版小册子，Project Gutenberg eBook #37537）
sources.quote: After the Earth jumped back on its track at 5:13:47 on the morning of Wednesday, April 18th, 1906, the citizens of San Francisco came down on their feet in fighting mood... The initial quake, being followed by many of less severity, tumbled chimneys, large and small buildings of poor or faulty construction, broke water mains and ruptured electric light and power conductors, causing many conflagrations in a few moments.

fact: 地震后的大火焚毁旧金山约七平方英里市区：在总人口约40万中近30万人无家可归，商业区几乎没有完整建筑残留；至少7.5万难民撤往奥克兰、伯克利、阿拉米达、贝尼西亚等湾对岸城市。

sources.title: Complete Story of the San Francisco Horror（Trumbull White、Richard Linthicum、Samuel Fallows，1906，Project Gutenberg eBook #26380）
sources.quote: Of its population of 400,000 nearly 300,000 were homeless. Gutted throughout its entire magnificent financial quarters by the swift work of thirty hours and with a black ruin covering more than seven square miles out into her very heart... The refugees numbered all told about 300,000. At least 75,000 of them made their way to Oakland, Berkeley, Alameda, Benicia and neighboring cities while many more fortunate and prosperous succeeded in reaching Los Angeles.

sources.title: San Francisco Relief Survey（Russell Sage Foundation, 1913，Project Gutenberg eBook #56217）
sources.quote: General Greely quoted the chief of the Census Bureau as giving 185,000 as the population of the burned area in 1900.

fact: 湾岸轮渡系统在震后运输难民：官方报告累计运送300,684人（其中约226,000人至湾岸周边城镇、67,000人至加州其他地点、7,684人至外州），1906年4月19日难民以平均每分钟70人的速度离开旧金山，该运输服务被估值456,000美元。

sources.title: San Francisco Relief Survey（Russell Sage Foundation, 1913，Project Gutenberg eBook #56217）
sources.quote: Suburban points around the bay 226,000 | Other points in California 67,000 | Other states 7,684 | Total 300,684... The value of this service, according to the official report, was $456,000. The report states that on April 19 the refugees, most of whom went to Oakland and adjoining communities, left San Francisco at the average rate of 70 per minute.

fact: 震后旧金山运输服务价格暴涨：雇一名马车夫带马和车每小时议价50美元，几条街区搬运行李箱收费20美元属常见；警察与军队可以凭枪口强制征用牲口车辆。

sources.title: Complete Story of the San Francisco Horror（Project Gutenberg eBook #26380）
sources.quote: It was impossible to secure a vehicle except at extortionate prices. One merchant engaged a teamster and horse and wagon, agreeing to pay $50 an hour. Charges of $20 for carrying trunks a few blocks were common. The police and military seized teams wherever they required them, their wishes being enforced at revolver point.

fact: 对94户在火灾前后均支付独立住所租金的家庭统计显示租金整体上移：月租40美元及以上的家庭由震前4户增至震后15户；震前最高月租45美元，震后最高65美元；月租20美元以上的家庭占比由45.7%升至53.2%。

sources.title: San Francisco Relief Survey（Russell Sage Foundation, 1913，Project Gutenberg eBook #56217，表52）
sources.quote: TABLE 52.--RESIDENCE RENTALS PAID, BEFORE AND AFTER THE FIRE, BY 94 FAMILIES... Less than $10: 13→14; $10 and less than $20: 38→30; $20 and less than $30: 26→23; $30 and less than $40: 13→12; $40 and over: 4→15. The highest rent paid before the fire was $45; after the fire, $65... Before the fire 45.7 per cent of the families paid a rental of $20 a month or more; after, 53.2 per cent were paying $20 or more.

fact: 救济营地居住成本可核算：1906年8月1日至1908年6月30日，官方营地共提供7,171,522人日居住，建造小屋与营房支出884,558.81美元、维护支出453,000.04美元，合计1,337,558.85美元，人均每日居住成本18.7美分（维护部分6美分）；计入军队提供的庇护作价421,195.08美元及1906年8月前支付的营地款项后，整个救济期营地相关总成本约2,101,284.09美元。

sources.title: San Francisco Relief Survey（Russell Sage Foundation, 1913，Project Gutenberg eBook #56217）
sources.quote: From August 1, 1906, to June 30, 1908, there is accurate information from which to determine the cost of the camps. During this period, 7,171,522 days' shelter was furnished at a cost of $884,558.81 for construction of cottages and of $453,000.04 for maintenance, a total of $1,337,558.85, a daily per capita cost of 18.7 cents... fact: 震后旧金山实行高强度治安管制：联邦军队由Funston少将指挥入城维持秩序，命令为“格杀勿论”式处置抢掠者——Morris记“strict command to shoot all looters at sight”，《Complete Story》记通告称“the orders are not to arrest but shoot down any one caught stealing”；离开城区者被禁止返回。

sources.title: Charles Morris, The San Francisco Calamity by Earthquake and Fire（1906，Project Gutenberg eBook #1560）
sources.quote: up from the military station at the Presidio... came at double quick a force of soldiers, under the efficient command of General Funston... These trained troops were at once put on guard over the city, with directions to keep the best order possible, and with strict command to shoot all looters at sight.

sources.title: Complete Story of the San Francisco Horror（Project Gutenberg eBook #26380）
sources.quote: you may be mistaken for one of the looters and shot on sight, as the orders are not to arrest but shoot down any one caught stealing... The soldiers enforced the rule against moving about except to escape the flames, and absolutely no one could enter the city who once had left.

fact: 地震当日市长Schmitz下令征用进入城市的全部食品物资并记账待偿，面包房被要求全力生产并将余量交给救济委员会——市政当局以强制手段接管食品分配。

sources.title: Charles Morris, The San Francisco Calamity by Earthquake and Fire（Project Gutenberg eBook #1560）
sources.quote: All the foodstuffs coming in on the cars were at once seized by order of the Mayor and added to the scanty supply, the names of the consignees being taken that this material might eventually be paid for. The bakers agreed to work their plants to their utmost capacity and to send all their surplus output to the relief committee.

fact: 保险业承受了巨额索赔：1906年出版物记载“some were forced into liquidation”，但全国金融形势未被击穿，“there was every reason to believe that the great bulk of the insurance would be paid”；同期资料将全市财产损失早期估计为2亿美元（后续研究通常给出更高数字，此处仅反映1906年当时口径）。

sources.title: Charles Morris, The San Francisco Calamity by Earthquake and Fire（Project Gutenberg eBook #1560）
sources.quote: companies were seriously crippled by the disaster and some were forced into liquidation. To the great relief of the entire country, nevertheless, the financial situation was not severely affected, and there was every reason to believe that the great bulk of the insurance would be paid.

sources.quote: Tremendous Loss of Life in Quake and Fire--Property Loss $200,000,000

fact: 旧金山救济与红十字基金的现金捐赠到1909年6月1日累计8,921,452.86美元（含利息等合计现金收入9,673,057.94美元），另有国会拨款2,500,000美元用于最初两个月的食物、衣物、寝具与庇护；对家庭的救济拨款中，最终获得500美元及以上援助的家庭仅647户（受助家庭共20,241户）。

sources.title: San Francisco Relief Survey（Russell Sage Foundation, 1913，Project Gutenberg eBook #56217）
sources.quote: TABLE 1.--CASH RECEIPTS OF THE FINANCE COMMITTEE OF RELIEF AND RED CROSS FUNDS... Cash donations, including San Francisco subscriptions and Red Cross remittances $8,921,452.86... Total cash receipts $9,673,057.94... The total cash donations... do not include the $2,500,000 appropriated by Congress... Eventually, of the 20,241 families assisted by the Committee, 647 families received as much as $500 each.

fact: 经济史研究将1906年旧金山大地震与1907年大恐慌联系起来：《Journal of Economic History》2004年论文题为“Real Shock, Monetary Aftershock: The 1906 San Francisco Earthquake and the Panic of 1907”；美联储历史文献同时记载1907年10月22日纽约活期贷款年化利率从9.5%跳升至70%，显示震后一年美国货币市场高度敏感。

sources.title: Federal Reserve History — The Panic of 1907（Jon R. Moen and Ellis W. Tallman），参考文献收录Odell & Weidenmier论文
sources.quote: Odell, Kerry A., and Marc D. Weidenmier. "Real Shock, Monetary Aftershock: The 1906 San Francisco Earthquake and the Panic of 1907." Journal of Economic History 64, no. 4 (December 2004): 1002-27.

sources.title: Federal Reserve History — The Panic of 1907
sources.quote: On the day Knickerbocker closed, October 22, the annualized rate jumped from 9.5 percent to 70 percent.

fact: 灭火手段包括定向爆破：军方派人在火线前方用炸药摧毁建筑制造隔离带，海军陆战队军士在夜间执行爆破作业，一次爆破即摧毁价值约100万美元的房屋以阻断火势。

sources.title: Charles Morris, The San Francisco Calamity by Earthquake and Fire（Project Gutenberg eBook #1560，第三章Fighting Flames with Dynamite）
sources.quote: The only hope that remained to the authorities was to endeavor to check the progress of the flames by the use of dynamite, blowing up buildings in the line of progress of the conflagration.

sources.title: Complete Story of the San Francisco Horror（Project Gutenberg eBook #26380）
sources.quote: Captain MacBride was in charge of the squad. Chief Gunner Adamson placed the charges... A million dollars' worth of property, noble residences and worthless shacks alike were blown to drifting dust, but that destruction broke the fire and sent the raging flames over their own charred path.

fact: 旧金山大火中美国铸币厂（United States Mint）建筑幸存，其金库内存有约3亿美元金银铸币与价值约800万美元的金银条块，成为灾后现金存量的关键节点。

sources.title: Charles Morris, The San Francisco Calamity by Earthquake and Fire（Project Gutenberg eBook #1560）
sources.quote: the escape of the United States Mint was one of the most remarkable incidents. Within the vaults of this fine structure was the vast sum of $300,000,000 in gold and silver coin and a value of $8,000,000 in bullion.

fact: 震毁建筑按结构类型统计共28,188栋：木框架建筑24,671栋、B/C级砖混建筑3,168栋、砖木混合259栋、A级防火（fireproof）建筑仅42栋、石质15栋、木质框架波纹铁皮33栋——既有建筑存量以木结构为绝对主体。

sources.quote: Character of buildings | Buildings destroyed: Wooden framed buildings 24,671; Brick--Classes B and C 3,168; Brick and wood (unclassified) 259; Fireproof--Class A 42; Stone 15; Corrugated iron (wooden frame) 33; Total 28,188.

fact: 灾后公共卫生以营地区卫生工程应对：截至1906年8月1日，营地与城市卫生工作支出155,473.60美元；营地设置储水消毒罐，幸存者日记描述日常风险包括持续煮沸水与牛奶以防热病（fever）。

sources.title: San Francisco Relief Survey（Russell Sage Foundation, 1913，Project Gutenberg eBook #56217）
sources.quote: Paid for sanitation of camps and city up to August 1, 1906: 155,473.60... lack of water for toilet appliances, the incessant boiling of water and milk for fear of fever, absence of light and means of transportation for some time...

fact: 旧金山日本侨民于1906年4月20日成立独立救济组织并合并为Japanese Relief Association，自行照料在美同胞；日本方面通过本地委员会与美国全国红十字会捐赠近25万美元，但救济调查同时记载社区存在“anti-Japanese feeling of a small but aggressive part of the community”。

sources.title: San Francisco Relief Survey（Russell Sage Foundation, 1913，Project Gutenberg eBook #56217）
sources.quote: Japan contributed directly to the local committee and through the American National Red Cross nearly a quarter of a million dollars. On April 20, independent relief associations were formed by Japanese residents in San Francisco and Oakland, but on the same day they wisely united under the name Japanese Relief Association to care for practically all their fellow countrymen.
